chunks: And whatever is in it from Al-Qasim ibn Burayd, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Al-Husayn Al-Sa'dawi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Qasim ibn Burayd ibn Muawiyah Al-Ajli.

key_terms.السَّعْدَاوِيِّ: Al-Sa'dawi, a nisba indicating origin or residence
key_terms.الْعَجَلِيِّ: Al-Ajli, a nisba indicating tribal affiliation
key_terms.الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ بُرَيْدٍ: Al-Qasim ibn Burayd, a prominent narrator
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect for companions or narrators

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Al-Qasim ibn Burayd verified in this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a precise biographical bridge, linking the early Kufan narrator Al-Qasim ibn Burayd to the contemporary scholarly circles of the late 3rd/early 4th century Hijri through a chain of trusted authorities like Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil. This specific isnad highlights the rigorous methodology of the Shia tradition in preserving oral transmissions across generations, ensuring that the reports of the Tabi'un are securely anchored in the reliable scholarly networks of the Imami community.
